Status.note: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists plant 55087, generator 1A, as operating. Operating since June 2001. An air permit staff report from November 2025 at https://mienviro.michigan.gov/ncore/downloadpdf/9126372892444753909 describes the plant as running with four turbines. No retirement, mothballing or sale was found.

Capacity (MW).note: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx gives 188.7 MW for generator 1A. A Consumers Energy press release from May 2025 at https://www.cmsenergy.com/investor-relations/news-releases/news-release-details/2025/Consumers-Energy-Expands-Zeeland-Natural-Gas-Plant-to-Grow-Michigans-Energy-Reliability/default.aspx says the turbine upgrades add 50 MW in total across the two simple cycle turbines. EIA has not yet raised the nameplate. GEM's 239 MW looks like 189 MW plus the whole 50 MW on one unit, which the release does not say. The EIA nameplate is the only per-unit figure found.

Equipment Manufacturer/Model.note: A Power Technology plant profile at https://www.power-technology.com/marketdata/power-plant-profile-zeeland-gas-turbine-power-plant-us/ says the Zeeland simple cycle turbines are two 7F.04 gas turbines of 188.7 MW each supplied by General Electric. The profile does not name the unit letters. The EIA-860M file lists both as 188.7 MW.

units.notes: Still operating. The upgrade was permitted in January 2025 and built by 2025. The per-unit nameplate after the upgrade was not found.
